PullRequest.Title: agentHost: use SDK-enabled reasoning summaries
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

The Copilot SDK now enables reasoning summaries, so VS Code no longer needs its own reasoning-summary override.

- Remove the experimental `chat.agentHost.copilot.reasoningSummary.enabled` setting, root configuration entry, settings forwarding, and launcher override.
- Let Copilot SDK sessions use the runtime's reasoning-summary default.
- Preserve GPT-5.6 medium verbosity, reasoning-effort controls, and Codex settings.
- Update regression coverage to verify both newly created and resumed sessions apply verbosity without overriding reasoning summaries.

## Validation

- 65 targeted launcher and settings-forwarding unit tests passed.
- Client transpilation and TypeScript type-check passed.
- ESLint and hygiene passed for all six changed files; commit hook passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Full Gulp compile was blocked by a local dependency mismatch: the branch declares Copilot runtime `1.0.85-unstable.r35379093703.g3514c9a`, while the installed SDK bundles `1.0.83`. The standalone client type-check passed.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: An experiment-enabled GPT-5.6 session issued a separate `options.update` RPC for reasoning summary after the already-awaited verbosity RPC, serially extending create/resume finalization before session initialization could continue.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Extra critical-path IPC latency during creation or resumption of experiment-enabled GPT-5.6 sessions.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: GPT-5.6 finalization now performs only the required medium-verbosity update and leaves reasoning-summary selection to the SDK default, removing one awaited runtime RPC from each affected create or resume launch.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 805 awaited `session.rpc.options.update({ reasoningSummary })`. `_finalizeSession` was awaited by both `_createSession` and resume paths, and `CopilotAgentSession.initializeSession` awaits `launcher.launch` before registering the SDK event interest or exposing the initialized session. The deleted `_applyGpt56Customizations` called verbosity first and then this reasoning-summary update, so experiment-enabled GPT-5.6 create/resume launches incurred an additional serialized RPC to the Copilot runtime subprocess. The updated create/resume test expectation drops exactly that fourth options update while retaining script-safety, sandbox, and verbosity updates.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or resume a Copilot SDK session using a GPT-5.6 model
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `CopilotAgentSession.initializeSession` awaits `CopilotSessionLauncher.launch`; create/resume and all `_finalizeSession` option updates must finish before event-interest registration and session registration can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create or resume the session through the Copilot SDK runtime subprocess.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one create or one resume per session; existing resume error fallback can add retries, unchanged by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same create/resume boundary and fallback behavior existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before session finalization starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update SDK runtime session options for script safety, sandbox configuration, and GPT-5.6 verbosity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: After the diff, three serialized option RPCs per GPT-5.6 launch; before, experiment-enabled launches performed a fourth reasoning-summary RPC. Non-GPT-5.6 and experiment-disabled cardinality is not increased.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Experiment-enabled GPT-5.6 create/resume launches additionally awaited `options.update({ reasoningSummary: 'concise' })` after verbosity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each awaited update extends session initialization before the wrapper is returned.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register SDK event-log interest after launcher completion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One registration per initialized session, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same registration followed launcher completion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs after the changed launcher path and remains required before session setup continues.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One unit of removed work per experiment-enabled GPT-5.6 session create or resume; there is no collection multiplier within a launch.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Within one launch, script-safety, sandbox, and verbosity option updates are serialized by `await`; the deleted reasoning-summary update was serialized after verbosity. Separate session launches may proceed independently, with no changed shared limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates in session option updates. Warm runtime state does not coalesce these per-session control-plane RPCs; the diff removes the redundant call entirely.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the deleted call is explicitly awaited on both create and resume finalization paths, and tests reduce the expected option-update sequence by exactly one.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The runtime RPC round-trip duration and population previously assigned the startup experiment are not measured in the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The diff improves affected launch latency; the concrete removed critical-path RPC was recorded as a regression fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench restoration and Copilot CLI root-setting forwarding to the local agent host
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The contribution is registered at `WorkbenchPhase.AfterRestored`; its asynchronous per-key reconciliation is therefore off the blocking restore/startup phases. Setting changes later trigger only their associated key push.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send a root-config change notification from the workbench client to the local agent host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one notification per advertised, changed key per reconciliation. The changed contribution now manages 10 keys instead of 11, so initial reconciliation can send one fewer notification; subsequent reasoning-summary setting notifications are removed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The reasoning-summary descriptor could add one notification on initial reconciliation or when its setting changed, subject to schema and structural-equality gates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fire-and-forget notification after workbench restoration; it does not block the restored workbench path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The fixed descriptor set and configuration-change frequency; effective cardinality decreases by one managed key.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Initial `_push` calls are launched independently without awaiting each other. Structural equality suppresses unchanged repeats, and the removed key eliminates one listener and one possible notification rather than increasing fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The current root-state value is the warm state. `structuralEquals` prevents dispatch when it already matches; absent schemas and undefined computed values are negative gates. Removing the key does not invalidate other entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the descriptor and trigger are deleted, while shared reconciliation and equality logic are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual host restarts and setting-change frequency vary, but the boundary count can only decrease.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Startup/listener work and possible renderer-to-host notification fan-out are reduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send GPT-5.6 model turns with SDK-managed reasoning summaries
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A turn still crosses the existing SDK/model network path. This diff changes no per-turn host loop or request scheduling; it stops overriding the SDK's reasoning-summary option during session launch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send model requests and receive streamed responses through the Copilot SDK runtime.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing model call per turn or SDK-requested subcall; no call is added, duplicated, or moved by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The SDK already handled model calls; the host optionally set a concise summary at launch for experiment-enabled sessions and otherwise left the SDK default in place.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The model request remains the turn's primary critical-path boundary, but the changed lines do not alter its count or scheduling.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of user turns and SDK subcalls, unchanged by the host-side deletion.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Model-call concurrency and turn serialization are unchanged by the removed launch-time override.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No changed cache key, prompt cache behavior, or request coalescing is evidenced. Summary policy is delegated to the runtime default.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for host-side cost: the diff only removes a launch-time options RPC and configuration plumbing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact SDK default summary representation is external to the repository, but no changed code adds per-turn serialization, model calls, or retained data.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Delegating summary policy does not itself establish increased token, rendering, or network work, while the only proven boundary change is a removed RPC.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and surrounding launch, protocol, and settings-forwarding paths. No diff-introduced performance finding met the reporting threshold. The PR removes one serialized Copilot runtime options RPC from affected GPT-5.6 launches and one potential root-config notification; the former was recorded as a concrete regression fix.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
